source: Vogel's Practical Organic Chemistry & Classic Natural Product Literature
description: Comprehensive authentic laboratory synthesis protocols for tropane alkaloids, classical organic transformations (Grignard, Diels-Alder, Fischer indole, Sandmeyer, Cannizzaro), and natural alkaloid extractions.

syntheses.description: Sir Robert Robinson's landmark 1917 biomimetic one-pot double-Mannich condensation forming the bicyclic tropane alkaloid core.
syntheses.literature_reference: Robinson, R. (1917). J. Chem. Soc., Trans., 111, 762-768; Vogel 5th ed.

workup.quench: Cool to room temperature (20 °C) in water bath
Spontaneous decarboxylation of intermediate tropinone dicarboxylic acid
workup.basification: Basify to pH 12 with 40% aqueous potassium hydroxide
workup.extraction: Extract 3x with 60 mL chloroform in separatory funnel
workup.drying: Dry organic extracts over anhydrous potassium carbonate (K2CO3)
workup.evaporation: Rotary evaporator at 45 °C and 50 mbar to yield crude orange oil
workup.purification: Vacuum distillation (bp 113 °C at 25 mmHg) or sublimation to give white crystalline needles

syntheses.description: Total chemical synthesis of the anticholinergic tropane alkaloid atropine via stereoselective reduction of tropinone followed by Fischer esterification with tropic acid.
syntheses.literature_reference: Willstätter, R. (1901). Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges., 34, 129; Vogel's Practical Organic Chemistry.

workup.quench: Cautiously quench excess sodium with water, acidify with HCl
workup.isolation: Extract neutral impurities with ether, basify aqueous layer with KOH and extract tropine with chloroform
workup.purification: Vacuum sublimation to yield pure tropine (mp 63 °C)

steps.name: Fischer Acid-Catalyzed Esterification with Tropic Acid

workup.isolation: Dissolve in dilute sulfuric acid, wash with ether, basify with ammonia to pH 9.5
workup.extraction: Extract atropine base with chloroform, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate
workup.recrystallization: Recrystallize from acetone/petroleum ether to give colorless lustrous needles (mp 115 °C)

syntheses.description: Quantitative extraction and isolation of pharmaceutical-grade tropane alkaloids from Atropa belladonna (Deadly Nightshade) dried leaves using Soxhlet percolation and acid-base partitioning.
syntheses.literature_reference: WHO Pharmacopoeia / European Pharmacopoeia Monographs on Belladonnae folium.

workup.concentration: Concentrate extract on rotary evaporator at 45 °C and 80 mbar to thick dark syrup
workup.notes: Exhaustive extraction verified by Meyer's reagent testing of siphon liquid.

workup.chlorophyll_removal: Wash acidic solution twice with 40 mL DCM to remove non-alkaloidal lipids and chlorophyll
workup.alkaloid_release: Basify aqueous layer with NH4OH to pH 10.0 to liberate free amine bases
workup.extraction: Extract free alkaloids 3x with 50 mL DCM in separatory funnel
workup.evaporation: Evaporate DCM on rotovap to yield pale yellow crystalline alkaloid cake
workup.purification: Dissolve in ethanol, titrate with sulfuric acid to obtain pharmaceutical atropine sulfate monohydrate

syntheses.description: Isolation of the anti-emetic and anticholinergic epoxide alkaloid scopolamine from Datura stramonium / Duboisia leaves followed by hydrobromide salt precipitation.
syntheses.literature_reference: Evans, W. C. (1979). The Tropane Alkaloids. Trease & Evans Pharmacognosy.

workup.filtration: Suction filtration through sintered glass funnel to remove leaf marc
workup.acid_transfer: Extract chloroform solution with three 60 mL portions of 0.2 M sulfuric acid

workup.precipitation: Dropwise addition of HBr to acetone solution triggers rapid crystallization of white scopolamine hydrobromide trihydrate
workup.filtration: Collect crystals on Büchner funnel, wash with cold acetone, vacuum dry (mp 195-199 °C)

syntheses.description: Preparation of phenylmagnesium bromide Grignard reagent from bromobenzene and magnesium turnings in anhydrous ether, followed by nucleophilic addition to methyl benzoate or benzophenone.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Section 5.17, p. 540-542.

workup.activation: Crush Mg turnings under ether with glass rod, add iodine crystal to initiate exothermic reflux
workup.addition: Add bromobenzene in ether dropwise to sustain gentle reflux until all magnesium dissolves

workup.quench: Pour into crushed ice with 10% H2SO4 to dissolve basic magnesium salts
workup.separation: Separate ethereal layer, wash with aqueous NaHCO3 and brine, dry over MgSO4
workup.crystallization: Distill off ether, recrystallize residue from boiling ethanol to afford colorless prisms (mp 162 °C)

syntheses.description: Concerted [4+2] cycloaddition of maleic anhydride to the 9,10-positions of anthracene in boiling xylene.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Section 7.5, p. 1115-1116.

workup.crystallization: Cool reaction flask in ice bath; adduct separates as heavy colorless needles
workup.filtration: Suction filtration on Büchner funnel, wash with 10 mL cold xylene then 15 mL petroleum ether
workup.purity_check: Melting point sharp at 262-263 °C, insolubility in petroleum ether confirms absence of unreacted anthracene

syntheses.description: Fischer indole synthesis involving condensation of cyclohexanone with phenylhydrazine in glacial acetic acid followed by sigmatropic rearrangement and cyclization with ammonia expulsion.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Section 8.4, p. 1161-1162.

workup.precipitation: Pour hot reaction mixture with vigorous stirring into 150 mL crushed ice/water
workup.filtration: Filter solid greenish-yellow crude mass, wash thoroughly with cold water
workup.recrystallization: Recrystallize from boiling ethanol (with decolourising charcoal) to yield glistening leaf-like prisms (mp 119 °C)

syntheses.description: Classical Sandmeyer reaction: Diazotization of aniline with sodium nitrite in aqueous hydrochloric acid, followed by copper(I) chloride catalyzed replacement of the diazonium group.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Section 6.13, p. 938-940.

workup.temperature_control: Maintain strictly between 0 °C and 5 °C by internal addition of crushed ice
workup.endpoint: Confirm free nitrous acid with starch-iodide test paper (faint blue spot)

steps.name: Copper(I) Chloride Catalyzed Substitution & Steam Distillation

workup.nitrogen_evolution: Slowly add cold diazonium solution to CuCl solution; nitrogen gas evolves briskly
workup.steam_distillation: Steam distill the mixture until no further oily droplets pass over
workup.separation: Separate lower organic chlorobenzene layer, wash with dilute NaOH then water, dry over anhydrous CaCl2
workup.distillation: Fractional distillation collecting pure fraction at 131-132 °C

syntheses.description: Base-catalyzed redox disproportionation of non-enolizable benzaldehyde yielding equal molar amounts of benzyl alcohol (reduced) and potassium benzoate (oxidized).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Section 6.25, p. 1029-1030.

workup.emulsion: Shake until stable emulsion forms, let stand overnight until solidified to potassium benzoate cake
workup.alcohol_isolation: Add 50 mL water, extract benzyl alcohol with three 25 mL portions of ether, dry over MgSO4 and distill (bp 205 °C)
workup.acid_isolation: Acidify remaining aqueous layer with conc. HCl to pH 1; pure benzoic acid precipitates as brilliant white plates (mp 122 °C)

syntheses.description: The classic Manske salt-fractionation protocol for the quantitative extraction and separation of beta-carboline alkaloids from Syrian Rue (Peganum harmala) seeds.
syntheses.literature_reference: Manske, R. H. F. (1927). J. Chem. Soc., 2496; Hasenfratz, V. (1927). Ann. Chim.

workup.filtration: Hot vacuum filtration through coarse filter to separate spent seeds
workup.concentration: Boil down combined decoctions to approx. 300 mL

workup.precipitation: Dissolve 100 g/L NaCl in boiling extract, cool slowly to 4 °C; harmine and harmaline hydrochlorides crystallize quantitatively as glowing yellow needles
workup.separation: Collect crystals, dissolve in water, adjust to pH 8.0 with NH4OH to precipitate pure harmine (mp 261 °C), then pH 10.5 to precipitate harmaline (mp 250 °C)

syntheses.description: Industrial and classical alkaloid extraction from Cinchona succirubra bark with slaked lime, toluene extraction, and selective crystallization as sparingly soluble neutral sulfate.
syntheses.literature_reference: Pelletier & Caventou (1820); British Pharmacopoeia monograph on Quinine.

workup.paste: Mix bark with lime and water to break tannin-alkaloid complexes
workup.extraction: Extract paste with hot toluene 3 times in water bath
workup.acid_transfer: Extract toluene layers with boiling dilute sulfuric acid

workup.neutralization: Neutralize hot acidic solution to exactly pH 6.0; quinine sulfate is uniquely insoluble in cold water (1:800)
workup.crystallization: Chilling deposits brilliant silky white needles of quinine sulfate, leaving cinchonine and quinidine in mother liquor
workup.fluorescence: Dissolving crystals in dilute H2SO4 displays intense blue UV fluorescence under 365 nm excitation

syntheses.description: Total semisynthetic protocol from Robinson tropinone via C-carbomethoxylation with dimethyl carbonate, stereoselective reduction to ecgonine methyl ester, and benzoylation.
syntheses.literature_reference: Findlay, S. P. (1954). J. Am. Chem. Soc., 76(11), 2855-2862; Casale, J. F. (1987). Forensic Sci. Int., 33(4), 275-298.

reagents.name: Sodium Hydride (60% dispersion in mineral oil)

workup.quench: Carefully quench excess NaH with dry methanol at 0 °C
workup.extraction: Extract 2-carbomethoxytropinone sodium salt into ice-cold water, wash with pentane to remove oil, acidify to pH 4

steps.name: Stereospecific Reduction to Ecgonine Methyl Ester

reagents.name: Sodium Amalgam (1.5% Na in Hg) or NaBH4/CeCl3

workup.basification: Basify to pH 10 with ammonium hydroxide at 0 °C
workup.extraction: Exhaustively extract with chloroform (5 x 50 mL), dry over anhydrous Na2SO4, evaporate to viscous ecgonine methyl ester oil

workup.quench: Pour into 100 mL cold water, basify with aqueous ammonia to pH 9
workup.crystallization: Extract with diethyl ether, wash with water, dry over K2CO3, evaporate and recrystallize from diethyl ether/petroleum ether to give white monoclinic prisms (mp 98 °C)

syntheses.description: Total organic chemical synthesis of the anticholinergic tropane alkaloid scopolamine from 6,7-dehydrotropinone via stereospecific epoxidation, carbonyl reduction, and esterification.
syntheses.literature_reference: Fodor, G. et al. (1959). J. Chem. Soc., 3461-3465; Vogel's Practical Organic Chemistry.

workup.quench: Wash organic layer with 10% sodium sulfite and saturated NaHCO3
workup.drying: Dry over anhydrous MgSO4 and concentrate under vacuum

workup.hydrolysis: Acidify with 2 M HCl to decompose boron complexes, basify with KOH to pH 11, extract with chloroform

workup.deacetylation: Mild alkaline hydrolysis (cold 1 M NaOH) of the phenolic acetate, followed by ether extraction to yield viscous crystalline scopolamine base

syntheses.description: Acetylation of aniline with acetic anhydride in sodium acetate buffer (Vogel 5th ed. p. 917).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 917.

workup.crystallization: Pour into 100 mL ice water; suction-filter lustrous white flakes; recrystallize from boiling water (mp 114 °C)

syntheses.description: Alkaline potassium permanganate oxidation of toluene to benzoic acid (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1029).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1029.

workup.acidification: Filter precipitated MnO2, acidify clear filtrate with concentrated HCl to pH 1; brilliant needle crystals of benzoic acid precipitate (mp 122 °C)

syntheses.description: Tin and hydrochloric acid reduction of nitrobenzene followed by steam distillation (Vogel 5th ed. p. 892).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 892.

workup.distillation: Cool, basify with 40% aqueous NaOH to dissolve stannate, steam-distill aniline, saturate distillate with NaCl, extract with ether, dry over KOH pellets, and distill (bp 184 °C)

syntheses.description: Vanadate-catalyzed nitric acid oxidation and ring cleavage of cyclohexanol (Vogel 5th ed. p. 668).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 668.

workup.crystallization: Maintain reaction temperature strictly between 55-60 °C with external ice bath; upon completion, chill in ice bath to deposit pure white crystals of adipic acid (mp 152 °C)

syntheses.description: Double Claisen-Schmidt aldol condensation of benzaldehyde with acetone in ethanolic sodium hydroxide (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1033).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1033.

workup.crystallization: Suction-filter yellow precipitate, wash with ice water and cold ethanol, recrystallize from ethyl acetate to yield bright yellow spangles (mp 111 °C)

syntheses.description: Cyanide- or thiamine-catalyzed umpolung condensation of two molecules of benzaldehyde (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1045).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1045.

workup.crystallization: Cool in ice bath; benzoin crystallizes as brilliant prisms; recrystallize from 95% ethanol (mp 133 °C)

syntheses.description: Nitric acid oxidation of alpha-hydroxyketone benzoin to alpha-diketone benzil (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1046).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1046.

workup.crystallization: Pour onto crushed ice; filter bright yellow oil which solidifies into crystals; recrystallize from ethanol (mp 95 °C)

syntheses.description: Base-catalyzed 1,2-phenyl migration (benzilic acid rearrangement) of benzil with potassium hydroxide (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1047).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1047.

workup.crystallization: Dilute with water, acidify with concentrated HCl; pure white benzilic acid precipitates as dense crystals (mp 150 °C)

syntheses.description: Classic Perkin reaction of benzaldehyde with acetic anhydride in the presence of anhydrous potassium acetate (Vogel 5th ed. p. 1037).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 1037.

workup.isolation: Steam-distill residual benzaldehyde, decolorize hot solution with active charcoal, acidify with HCl; cinnamic acid crystallizes as glistening needles (mp 133 °C)

syntheses.description: Synthesis of the chemiluminescent reagent from 3-nitrophthalic acid via hydrazine cyclization and sodium dithionite reduction (Vogel 5th ed. p. 924).
syntheses.literature_reference: Huntress, E. H. et al. (1934). J. Am. Chem. Soc., 56(1), 241-242; Vogel's Practical Organic Chemistry.

workup.quench: Heat to 215 °C to flash-boil water, cool to 100 °C, pour into 50 mL hot water; filter 3-nitrophthalhydrazide cake

workup.precipitation: Boil 5 min, acidify with glacial acetic acid to pH 5; luminol separates as pale yellow microcrystalline powder displaying bright blue chemiluminescence when oxidized with H2O2/K3[Fe(CN)6]

syntheses.description: Zinc chloride catalyzed melt condensation of phthalic anhydride with resorcinol at 180 °C (Vogel 5th ed. p. 986).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 986.

workup.crushing: Heat in oil bath until viscous red melt solidifies; cool, crush cake, boil with dilute HCl to remove zinc salts; collect reddish-brown fluorescein powder (mp 314 °C)

syntheses.description: Tetrabromination of fluorescein with elemental bromine in ethanol followed by disodium salt formation (Vogel 5th ed. p. 988).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 988.

workup.neutralization: Drop bromine slowly into stirred fluorescein suspension; filter tetrabromofluorescein, convert to disodium salt with Na2CO3; precipitates as bronze-colored crystals with green sheen

syntheses.description: Diazotization of sulfanilic acid and azo coupling with N,N-dimethylaniline (Vogel 5th ed. p. 951).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 951.

workup.crystallization: Diazotize at 0-5 °C, add dimethylaniline in dilute acetic acid, basify with 10% NaOH to precipitate orange-gold plates of methyl orange; recrystallize from water

syntheses.description: Diazotization of aniline and azo coupling with alkaline 2-naphthol (Vogel 5th ed. p. 949).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 949.

workup.precipitation: Pour cold benzenediazonium chloride into alkaline 2-naphthol solution; brick-red dye separates immediately; suction-filter and recrystallize from glacial acetic acid (mp 134 °C)

syntheses.description: Three-step synthesis from acetanilide via chlorosulfonation, ammonolysis, and selective acid deacetylation (Vogel 5th ed. p. 883).
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman, p. 883.

workup.quench: Pour onto crushed ice; collect sulfonyl chloride cake

workup.neutralization: Heat with ammonia to form sulfonamide, boil with 3 M HCl to hydrolyze acetyl group, neutralize hot with NaHCO3; sulfanilamide crystallizes as pure white needles (mp 165 °C)

syntheses.description: Exhaustive Soxhlet extraction of powdered black pepper (Piper nigrum) with 95% ethanol, resin precipitation with KOH, and recrystallization.
syntheses.literature_reference: Ikan, R. (1991). Natural Products: A Laboratory Guide, 2nd ed., Academic Press; Vogel 5th ed.

workup.crystallization: Soxhlet-extract for 3 h, concentrate to 30 mL, add 10% alcoholic KOH, filter resinous precipitate; dilute filtrate with water, chill overnight to obtain yellow monoclinic needles of piperine (mp 130 °C)

syntheses.description: Direct atmospheric steam distillation of orange peel (Citrus sinensis) flavedo with optical purity verification.
syntheses.literature_reference: Pavia, D. L. et al. (2012). Introduction to Organic Laboratory Techniques, Brooks/Cole.

workup.separation: Distill until 100 mL distillate is collected; separate top terpene layer in separatory funnel, extract aqueous phase with 20 mL pentane, combine and dry over anhydrous MgSO4, evaporate pentane to give optically pure (+)-limonene ([alpha]D = +115°)

syntheses.description: Steam distillation of cloves (Syzygium aromaticum) followed by selective acid-base extraction separating phenol from caryophyllene.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th Ed., Longman.

workup.partition: Steam-distill 150 mL milky clove oil distillate; extract into ether; deprotonate eugenol with 5% KOH into aqueous layer; separate and wash neutral terpenes; re-acidify aqueous layer with 6 M HCl to liberate pure eugenol; extract with ether, dry over MgSO4, evaporate

syntheses.description: Ethanolic Soxhlet extraction of dried chili peppers (Capsicum frutescens), defatting against hexane, and silica gel column chromatography.
syntheses.literature_reference: Govindarajan, V. S. (1986). Capsicum — production, technology, chemistry, and quality. Part III. CRC Crit. Rev. Food Sci. Nutr., 24(3), 207-288.

workup.column: Evaporate ethanol extract, partition against hexane/water to remove carotenes and fats; flash-chromatograph on silica gel (EtOAc/Hexane 1:1) to yield crystalline capsaicin (mp 65 °C, extreme irritant)

syntheses.description: Alkaline steam distillation of tobacco leaves (Nicotiana tabacum), extraction into ether, and picrate salt crystallization.
syntheses.literature_reference: Vogel's Practical Organic Chemistry; Pictet & Rotschy (1904). Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges., 37, 1225.

workup.crystallization: Distill with steam until distillate no longer gives alkaloid precipitate with Mayer's reagent; extract with ether, dry over KOH pellets, and treat with saturated ethanolic picric acid to form yellow needles of nicotine dipicrate (mp 218 °C)

syntheses.description: Historical Gregory water process: hot aqueous extraction of opium latex, meconate removal with calcium chloride, and selective base precipitation at pH 9.1.
syntheses.literature_reference: Gregory, W. (1831). Edinb. Med. Surg. J., 35, 331; Barbier, A. (1947). Bull. Narc., 2(3), 22-29.

workup.filtration: Boil with water, add CaCl2 to quantitatively precipitate insoluble calcium meconate, filter, concentrate mother liquor to crystallize the double salt of morphine and codeine hydrochlorides (Gregory salt)

workup.isolation: Redissolve Gregory salt, add dilute ammonia to exactly pH 9.1; amphoteric morphine base precipitates quantitatively while mono-phenolic codeine remains in solution; filter and dry (mp 255 °C dec)

syntheses.description: Selective quick acetone wash of Salvia divinorum leaves, active carbon decolorization, and recrystallization from isopropanol.
syntheses.literature_reference: Ortega, A. et al. (1982). J. Chem. Soc., Perkin Trans. 1, 2505-2508; Valdés, L. J. et al. (1984). J. Org. Chem., 49(24), 4716-4720.

workup.crystallization: Macerate leaves for only 2 min to selectively dissolve peltate glandular trichomes without leaching cellular chlorophyll; stir with charcoal, filter, evaporate acetone, recrystallize residue from boiling isopropanol to yield colorless rhombic prisms of pure Salvinorin A (mp 242 °C)
